item.title: Modern C++ Memory Management in 2026: unique_ptr, shared_ptr, and When You Still Need Raw Pointers
item.description: I still see pull requests in 2026 with a raw new sitting in a constructor and no matching delete anywhere in sight. Nobody’s being careless — the codebase just grew organically and smart pointers never made it into the house style. So here’s the practical version of “modern C++ memory management” I wish someone had handed me years ago: not a language-lawyer tour of the standard, just what to reach for, when, and why the alternative bites you eventually.
